title: RD-MT163-SteeringTranscripts

scope.summary:
GOAL: Make session transcripts capture the FULL steering exchange — injected steer messages, acks, interrupts, resumes, notifications, and structured signals — so a replayed session shows not only what the model said but what it was TOLD and WHEN. Transcript export gains a steering timeline; the React SessionReplayPanel and the native replay surface render that timeline READ-ONLY. Transcripts are the governed custody surface for steer TEXT (the ledgers of MT-162 hold only hashes; FR events of MT-161 hold hashes/previews).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) additive variants on SessionTranscriptEntry + mapping/merge/filter/search updates in src/backend/handshake_core/src/session_transcript/mod.rs; (b) steering-timeline section in src/backend/handshake_core/src/session_transcript/export.rs; (c) replay integration so checkpoint-replayed sessions reconstruct the steering entries (session_checkpoint/replay.rs read + minimal wiring if a new entry kind must pass through); (d) React: app/src/components/session/SessionReplayPanel.tsx extended with a read-only steering timeline lane (NAMED allowed exception to the app/src/** freeze); (e) native replay surface extension in src/frontend/handshake_native (steering timeline rendering in the existing session replay/diagnostics surface, swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs pattern); (f) tests for mapping, merge ordering, export, and searchability.

DETAILED SPEC — TRANSCRIPT ENTRY EXTENSIONS (session_transcript/mod.rs; SessionTranscriptEntry enum at line 89, TranscriptKind at line 58 — ALL changes additive; existing variants, seq/timestamp/kind accessors lines 179-227, and wire compatibility for previously persisted transcripts are preserved):

New SessionTranscriptEntry variants (serde-tagged consistently with the existing enum; each carries seq: u64, at_utc: DateTime<Utc> like its siblings):
  1. SteerInjected { message_id, sender: SteerSender (Operator | Session { session_id } | Role { role_id }), text: String, payload_sha256: String } — the sha256 MUST equal the MT-162 ledger row hash, making transcript text verifiable against the ledger.
  2. SteerAcked { message_id, ack_kind: String }.
  3. SteerRejected { message_id, reason: String }.
  4. InterruptRequested { message_id, requested_by: SteerSender }.
  5. InterruptConfirmed { message_id, exit_code: Option<i32> }.
  6. SessionResumed { resume_kind: String, prior_turn_count: u64 }.
  7. StructuredSignal { signal_kind: String, wp_id: Option<String>, mt_id: Option<String>, body_sha256: String } — MT-loop signals (FR-EVT-MT-SIGNALED).
  8. Notification { message_id, notify_kind: String, text: String } — m2m notifications (FR-EVT-M2M-NOTIFY).
New TranscriptKind values mirroring the variants (steer, interrupt, resume, signal, notification) with from_ipc coverage (line 72).

FR-EVENT MAPPING: extend entries_from_fr_event (line 339) to map the MT-161 catalogue: FR-EVT-SESSION-STEER-{QUEUED->SteerInjected, ACKED->SteerAcked, REJECTED->SteerRejected}, FR-EVT-SESSION-INTERRUPT-{REQUESTED,CONFIRMED}, FR-EVT-SESSION-RESUMED, FR-EVT-M2M-{STEER->SteerInjected(sender=Session), NOTIFY->Notification}, FR-EVT-MT-SIGNALED->StructuredSignal. FR payloads carry hashes, not text — the mapping produces hash-only entries; full text enters the transcript at the live capture point (the steering runtime family MT-002/MT-008 appends SteerInjected with text at delivery time). entries_from_fr_event stays lossless and total: unknown FR-EVT ids keep the existing defensive fallthrough behavior, never panic.

MERGE + ORDER: merge_transcript (line 443) must interleave steering entries with chat/tool entries in stable seq order, deduplicating by (kind, message_id) so a live-appended SteerInjected and its FR-derived hash-only twin collapse to the richer (text-bearing) entry. searchable_text (line 557) includes steer/notification text so replay search finds steering content. filter_by_kinds (line 529) supports the new kinds.

EXPORT (export.rs): the transcript export gains a 'steering_timeline' section: ordered array of { seq, at_utc, kind, message_id, sender, ack_state (joined from entry pairs), text_or_sha256 } — machine-readable, plus inclusion in any existing human-readable rendering the exporter already produces. Export of a session with zero steering events emits an empty timeline (not a missing key).

GUI READ SURFACES (both READ-ONLY — no steering controls here; interactive steering UI belongs to the session/steering families):
- React SessionReplayPanel.tsx: render the steering timeline as a distinct lane/track in the replay — injected messages, acks, interrupts, resumes visibly typed (icon/label per kind), clicking an entry reveals full text (when present) and correlation ids. No new write calls; consumes existing replay/export data.
- Native: extend the existing native session replay/diagnostics surface following the swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs pattern (stable element ids for parallel-model GUI testing, HBR-SWARM discipline) to list the same timeline read-only.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read the grounding files first: session_transcript/mod.rs in full (entry enum 89, kind 58, from_ipc 72, entries_from_fr_event 339, merge_transcript 443, append_terminal_scrollback 497, filter_by_kinds 529, searchable_text 557), session_transcript/export.rs, session_checkpoint/{replay.rs,checkpoint.rs,writer.rs} (how entries survive checkpoint/replay), app/src/components/session/SessionReplayPanel.tsx, src/frontend/handshake_native/src/swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs, MT-161 contract (FR ids + payload fields), MT-162 contract (payload_sha256 custody split).
2. Add the 8 variants + kinds additively; update every exhaustive match the compiler flags (accessors, filter, search, merge) — compiler-driven, no wildcard-arm shortcuts that would silently drop new kinds from search/filter.
3. Extend entries_from_fr_event with the MT-161 mapping; property: every mapped entry preserves message_id and timestamps from the FR payload.
4. Implement merge dedup by (kind, message_id) preferring text-bearing entries; keep ordering stable and deterministic for identical inputs.
5. Extend export.rs with steering_timeline; keep the existing export shape backward-compatible (only additive keys).
6. Verify checkpoint replay: a session checkpointed after steering events replays with the steering entries intact (test via session_checkpoint replay path; wire-through only if the replay path filters kinds).
7. React: add the read-only steering lane to SessionReplayPanel.tsx with stable data-testid attributes per entry kind; no other app/src file changes.
8. Native: add the read-only timeline listing to the native replay/diagnostics surface with stable element ids.
9. Tests: backend mapping/merge/export/search tests + a React component test for the steering lane rendering a fixture timeline + native surface smoke coverage per the crate's existing GUI-test conventions.

acceptance_criteria: SessionTranscriptEntry gains exactly the 8 contracted steering variants additively; previously persisted transcript JSON still deserializes (backward-compat test with a pre-change fixture).
entries_from_fr_event maps every steering-relevant MT-161 id to the correct entry kind, preserves message_id/timestamps, and keeps the defensive unknown-id fallthrough (totality test).
SteerInjected.payload_sha256 equals the MT-162 ledger hash for the same message (cross-check test computing sha256 of the text).
merge_transcript interleaves steering entries in stable seq order and dedups (kind, message_id) pairs preferring text-bearing entries (determinism test: same input twice -> identical output).
searchable_text and filter_by_kinds cover the new kinds (search finds steer text; filter isolates the steering lane).
Export contains a machine-readable steering_timeline section, present-and-empty for sessions without steering; existing export keys unchanged (additive-only diff proven by fixture comparison).
A checkpointed-then-replayed session retains its steering entries (replay round-trip test).
SessionReplayPanel renders the steering timeline read-only with stable data-testid per entry kind; component test passes; no steering-control (write) elements exist in the panel.
Native replay/diagnostics surface lists the same timeline read-only with stable element ids.
cargo build green, clippy clean; React build/tests green for the touched component.

implementation_notes: Custody split (do not blur it): transcript = governed full text; MT-162 ledger = hash + ack state; MT-161 FR = hash/preview + correlation. The sha256 equality test is the seam that keeps all three honest.

Live text capture point: the steering runtime (session family MT-002/MT-008) appends the text-bearing SteerInjected at delivery time; this MT provides the entry types, FR mapping, merge dedup, export, and read surfaces. If the session family lands after this MT, the text-bearing path is proven here with a direct-append test rather than the live runtime.

READ-ONLY is a contract line for both GUI surfaces: no send/steer/interrupt buttons in the replay panel — interactive steering UI is owned by the steering/session families; adding controls here would duplicate a surface and violate the family split.

Follow the existing native GUI conventions from swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs (stable ids, non-focus-stealing rendering, HBR-QUIET) — the replay surface must never pop or grab focus during parallel-model test runs.

Unknown-kind fallthrough in entries_from_fr_event is a shipped defensive contract (agent_activity-style losslessness); keep it total — WP-017 families may add FR kinds later (additive), and old builds must not panic on them.

surfaces: app/src/components/session/SessionReplayPanel.tsx (read-only steering timeline lane — extension of an existing surface, not a new pane)
src/frontend/handshake_native session replay/diagnostics surface (read-only timeline listing)
gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Per the RD family split, the WP-017 GUI obligation (new operator pane + Argus coverage) is carried by MT-166's audit pane. This MT only extends existing replay surfaces read-only; their rendering is proven by component/native tests and the exported timeline is trace-projection reconstructable.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Replay-surface behavior is documented in the MT-165 manual entries (session replay + steering timeline section); MT-165 defines the entry set and the conformance check this MT's surfaces are checked against.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: flight_recorder: WIRED — consumes MT-161 kinds via entries_from_fr_event; transcript entries are FR-correlated by message_id
internal_diagnostics: typed DEFERRED(reason=WP-KERNEL-015-not-shipped) unless the internal_diagnostics tier exists at implementation time; disposition recorded by MT-164
palmistry: typed DEFERRED(reason=WP-KERNEL-015-not-shipped) unless Palmistry exists at implementation time; disposition recorded by MT-164
risk_if_missed: Replay shows only model output: operators cannot see what a session was told, when it was interrupted, or why it resumed; steering disputes are unverifiable (no text custody surface), and the MT-166 audit pane has no drill-down target for message content.

risks: RISK-1: Wire break — new enum variants or kind strings break deserialization of previously persisted transcripts/checkpoints, corrupting historical replay.
RISK-2: Dedup swallows truth — the (kind, message_id) merge dedup collapses genuinely distinct entries (e.g. re-delivered steer after resume), hiding a delivery from the timeline.
RISK-3: Read-only erosion — a 'small' resend button lands in the replay panel, creating an unowned steering write path that bypasses the session family's queue/ledger discipline.
RISK-4: Hash mismatch — transcript text and ledger hash diverge (encoding, trimming, normalization) so the verification seam between MT-162 and MT-163 always fails or, worse, is skipped.
RISK-5: Search/filter holes — wildcard match arms silently exclude new kinds from searchable_text/filter_by_kinds, making steering content invisible to replay search.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): backward-compat fixture test with pre-change persisted JSON; additive serde tags only; checkpoint replay round-trip test.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): dedup keys include seq-window semantics — only an FR-derived hash-only entry and its live text twin for the SAME message_id and same delivery collapse; a re-delivery mints a new message_id upstream (MT-162 contract), tested with a re-delivery fixture.

CTRL-3 (RISK-3): acceptance criterion asserts no write/control elements in the panel; component test queries for absence of button roles in the steering lane; contract names the owning families for interactive UI.

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): one canonical hashing rule (sha256 over exact UTF-8 payload bytes, no trim/normalize) stated here and in MT-162; cross-check test computes the hash from transcript text and matches the ledger row.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): compiler-driven exhaustiveness — no new wildcard arms in the touched matches; explicit tests assert search hits and filter inclusion per new kind.

corrections: Stub asked for 'SessionReplayPanel (React) + native replay surface extended' — confirmed SessionReplayPanel.tsx exists at the briefed path and swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs is the native pattern file; both are named allowed exceptions, everything else in app/src/** stays frozen.

Refined the custody model against the code: FR payloads are hash/preview-redacted (duckdb.rs redaction, MT-161), so transcripts are designated the sole full-text custody surface, and the FR->entry mapping is hash-only with live capture supplying text — this resolves the otherwise-contradictory 'transcripts capture full exchange' vs 'FR never stores raw text'.
Verified entries_from_fr_event exists (line 339) and already implements defensive FR-event mapping — the contract extends it rather than inventing a parallel mapper.
